slides.text:
`defer` schedules a call. It runs when the surrounding function returns, by whichever `return` it leaves.

The snippet is pseudo code, not Go.
slides.code:
function runs:
    schedule cleanup for the end
    step one
    step two
function returns -> cleanup runs

slides.text:
The usual use pairs a resource with its release: open it, check the error, defer the close on the next line.

`f` is the open file: `f.Close()` releases it and `f.Name()` gives its name.

The snippet is pseudo code, not Go.
slides.code:
f = open(path)
if open failed: return
defer close(f)
use f

exercises.title: Which defers are registered?
exercises.guide: Read the code, then pick the output. Each value prints on its own line.
options: in stock, checked, --, in stock, checked
exercises.explanation: A `defer` counts only once its line runs. `check(0)` returns before the second one, so only "checked" runs. After the `--`, `check(2)` runs both, last in first out.

slides.text: `defer` needs a call, not a function. To defer a function literal, call it: the `()` after the closing brace is required.
